name: Western Ghats
description: The Western Ghats are a 1,600-km chain of forested mountains running down India's west coast, from Gujarat to the southern tip of the peninsula. They are older than the Himalaya and peak at Anamudi, nearly 2,700 m high. By catching the monsoon rains, they shape the climate of the region. Their evergreen forests shelter at least 325 globally threatened species.
